title: Can all eight angles of a transversal be different?
description: A line crosses two lines and makes eight angles. The board pairs up the angles that face each other, finds at most four different measures, and then shows that angles two and four make five angles that cannot all differ. Keeko doubts that eight angles can all differ.
teaching_notes: One idea: angles that face each other across a crossing are equal, so eight angles from a transversal give at most four different measures. Watch for students who count eight angles and expect eight measures.

source: A transversal t crosses lines l and m. The angles are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 going round the crossing with l, and 5, 6, 7, 8 going round the crossing with m in the same way. Can all eight angles have different measures? Can the five angles 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2 be all different?
video_script.why: The child uses equal facing angles to see how many different measures a transversal can make.
video_script.substitution: The book's own question about the eight angles made when one line crosses two lines, and the five angles six, five, four, three and two.
video_script.anchor: Two lines l and m crossed by a line t, with the eight angles numbered one to eight.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks eight angles must give eight different measures.
video_script.payoff_line: No, the eight angles have at most four different measures.

final_answer.value: No: at most four different measures; and 2 and 4 are equal, so the five cannot all be different
final_answer.spoken: no, the eight angles have at most four different measures, and angles two and four are equal, so the five angles cannot all be different

hold_back: No: at most four different measures; and 2 and 4 are equal, so the five cannot all be different
maths_rules: a line that crosses two lines is a transversal and makes eight angles
vertically opposite angles are equal: 1 and 3, 2 and 4, 5 and 7, 6 and 8
four pairs of equal angles give at most 4 different measures, so the eight angles cannot all differ
among the five angles 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2, the angles 2 and 4 are a vertically opposite pair, so they are equal and the five cannot all differ
the slip: eight angles do not need eight measures, because facing angles share a measure
video_script.design: One figure stays on the stage with the eight angles numbered. The facing pairs light up in pairs, and the five angles are picked out at the end.
